newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia little affected by GSP withdrawal - PM.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia little affected by GSP withdrawal - PM.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday the U.S. withdrawal of Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) privileges will have little impact on the local industry.

"We do realise that one day Malaysia will lose its GSP status and that is why we have always urged industries to be more efficient," he told reporters after after launching Malaysia's first locally made motorcycle at Gurun in northern Perak state.
"Many of these privileges are enjoyed by American companies that have production facilities here for re-export back to the United States," he said.
He said Malaysia was increasing its trade with other countries such as China and Japan, which would further reduce the impact of the loss of GSP status.

The prime minister's comments followed an incorrect report by a news agency from Washington that quoted Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky as saying that Malaysia would be graduated from the GSP next week.
A U.S. embassy spokesman told Reuters this was not true. Malaysia would move out of the system only on January 1, 1997.
"There will be a presidential proclamation issued in about a week which graduates Malaysia from this programme starting January 1, 1997," Barshefsky said in Washington.
Under the GSP, nations are allowed to export a specified list of goods at zero or subsidised tariff.
